chunks: Ali (ibn al-Husayn) from his father from Hammad from Aban ibn Taghlib said:
Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'The portion is one of ten, because the mountains were ten and the birds four.'
ai.seo_question: What is the rationale for khums being one-fifth according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him) elucidates the rationale behind the one-fifth share (khums) by linking it to a cosmological framework of ten mountains and four birds. This reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of deriving legal rulings from natural signs and divine order, emphasizing that the division of wealth is not arbitrary but rooted in the structure of creation.
